overview: 99 official Group 1 Prelims questions (2008–2024) – the heaviest science block. 80 are 'S&T in daily life' one-liners (units, alloys, household chemicals, plant parts, body facts); 12 test institutes/programmes (location, parent ministry, lead partners); scientists, STI policy and 'nature of science' are thin. Since 2023 the format shifts to statement-based and multiple-correct items on recent DST/CSIR/ICMR news.

possibility.angle: Everyday physics: units, instruments, optics, mechanics
possibility.evidence: part of E18/2 (80 Qs, all six years 2008–2024); e.g. 2008 Angstrom/decibel/pascal, 2010 momentum-KE, 2019 rainbow and rear-view mirror
possibility.what_they_ask: unit of a quantity, what a device does (diode, transformer), which phenomenon (rainbow, inertia), simple ratio (KE ∝ p²)

possibility.angle: Everyday chemistry: household substances, alloys, gases, water hardness
possibility.what_they_ask: chemical name of a common substance (laughing gas, milk of magnesia, gun cotton), alloy composition (brass), use (sodium benzoate preservative, PTFE non-stick), cause (permanent hardness = sulphates)

possibility.angle: Everyday biology: plant parts, pigments, body organs, enzymes, vitamins
possibility.what_they_ask: edible/economic part (ginger rhizome, chicory root), pigment colour (lutein yellow, tomato carotenoids), organ fact (liver largest gland, cornea donated), enzyme in tears

possibility.angle: Recent Indian health/tech devices and products
possibility.what_they_ask: what the device/product does, which institution developed it, which harmful chemical was banned

location of a research institute (NIO Goa, CPCRI Kasaragod, CTRI Rajahmundry, CCMB/ICRISAT Hyderabad), attached-office status (NATMO–DST), lead partners of a mega-project (LIGO-India), DST women's schemes (WIDUSHI)

possibility.angle: National Policy on STI and India's innovation rankings (E18/3)
possibility.what_they_ask: which schemes target brain drain (VAJRA, Ramanujan, INSPIRE), India's rank and publisher of each innovation index; STIP 2020 draft goals are the natural next target

possibility.angle: Prominent Indian scientists, prizes and days (E18/5)
possibility.what_they_ask: why 28 Feb is National Science Day (Raman Effect), Bhatnagar Prize winners, women 'firsts' in science

possibility.evidence: 1 Q: 2010 (ethology); other APPSC exams ask -ology names (rheology, axiology, etymology)
possibility.what_they_ask: name of a branch of study; scientific method steps

traps.trap: [E18/2] Unit swapped with a quantity of the same family
traps.spot: 'X is a unit of' with options all physical quantities (time/length/weight)
traps.fix: Know the dimension: angstrom = length (10⁻¹⁰ m), decibel = sound level, pascal = pressure

traps.spot: biology vs chemistry term for the same idea (endergonic vs endothermic)
traps.fix: Bioprocess language uses energy (endergonic/exergonic); heat language (endo/exothermic) is chemistry
traps.pyq: 'bioprocess by absorption of energy' → Endergonic, not Endothermic [group1-prelims-2008#131]

traps.fix: Bicarbonates = temporary (removed by boiling); sulphates/chlorides of Ca, Mg = permanent
Brass = Cu + Zn; bronze = Cu + Sn; German silver = Cu + Zn + Ni
traps.pyq: 'Brass is an alloy of' → Copper and Zinc [group1-prelims-2010#133]

traps.trap: Institute moved to a wrong but plausible state/city
traps.spot: location question on a coastal/agri institute; options are neighbouring states or cities
traps.fix: Tie the institute to its crop/ecosystem: CPCRI coconut → Kasaragod; CTRI tobacco → Rajahmundry; NIO → Goa; ARIES → Nainital
traps.pyq: 'Sampurnanand Telescope … ARIES, Ladakh' → ARIES is at Nainital [group1-prelims-2023-paper2#74]

traps.trap: Organ/function swap in a device description
traps.spot: a name clue (ARTSENS = arteries) paired with a different organ or a famous but wrong institution
traps.fix: Decode the acronym, then check the developer; organ swap usually travels with an institution swap
traps.pyq: 'ARTSENS … neurons … developed by NIMHANS' → arteries, IIT Madras [group1-prelims-2024-paper2#81]

traps.trap: Two-partner option with one wrong partner
traps.spot: options 'A in collaboration with B' where A repeats across options
traps.fix: Fix the lead first, then check the partner (AIIMS + C-DAC, not CAIR)

traps.spot: multiple-correct list of genuine schemes, one with a different target group
traps.fix: Ask whom the scheme brings in: ASEAN-India fellowship brings ASEAN researchers – not reversing India's brain drain
traps.pyq: brain-gain schemes → VAJRA, Ramanujan, INSPIRE only [group1-prelims-2023-paper2#79]

traps.trap: Famous-but-wrong discovery for a day or prize
traps.spot: options are all real Indian achievements (J.C. Bose, Aryabhata, Apsara)
traps.fix: 28 February = C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect (1928)
traps.pyq: 'National Science Day … to mark the' → Raman Effect [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#66]

techniques.name: [E18/2] Dimension check
techniques.how: Before reading options, say what the quantity measures; strike any option of another dimension.
techniques.example: 'Pressure is measured in' – mass/volume is density, degrees is angle/temperature, watt is power → Pascal [group1-prelims-2008#126]

techniques.name: Formula-scaling
techniques.how: Write the relation, scale the variable, compute the % change; avoid linear guesses.
techniques.example: KE = p²/2m; p ×2 → KE ×4 → increase 300% (100%, 200% fall) [group1-prelims-2010#129]

techniques.name: Name-root decoding
techniques.how: Break Greek/Latin roots or product acronyms to get the subject.
techniques.example: 'Chiral' – chir = hand (as in chiropractor) → Hand [group1-prelims-2008#130]; 'Ethology' = ethos/behaviour vs etymology = words [group1-prelims-2010#141]

techniques.name: Parent-body elimination for institute lists
techniques.how: Identify the parent ministry of the project; strike institutes under another ministry.
techniques.example: LIGO-India is DAE + DST → IIST (Dept of Space) and an unknown private observatory fall → IPR, IUCAA, RRCAT [group1-prelims-2024-paper2#71]

techniques.name: Statement-by-statement truth with 'incorrect' flip
techniques.how: Mark T/F on each line, then re-read whether the stem asks correct or incorrect; 'None of the above' is valid when all are true.
techniques.example: GII 40, WIPO 7th, NRI 60, IP Index 42/55 all true; stem asks 'incorrect' → None of the above [group1-prelims-2024-paper2#69]

techniques.name: Everyday-observation reasoning
techniques.how: Picture the real object; good conductors lose heat fastest, convex mirrors shrink images.
techniques.example: Rear-view mirror is convex → image diminished → magnification less than one [group1-prelims-2019-paper2#64]; metal cup conducts → tea cools fastest [group1-prelims-2010#127]

confusions.remember: Endergonic = free energy absorbed (bio); endothermic = heat absorbed (chem)
Lactometer = milk purity (density); hygrometer = humidity; hydrometer = liquid density in general
Tears kill bacteria with lysozyme; amylase digests starch
Sampurnanand 104-cm telescope = ARIES, Nainital; Hanle observatory = IIA Bengaluru's
Hyderabad = cell biology + semi-arid crops; coast = oceanography + coconut
Headlight focuses (concave); rear-view widens field, diminished image (convex)
Anandibai = first woman doctor of Western medicine (MD 1886); Sohonie = science PhD (1939), as keyed

anchors: 28 February – National Science Day: Raman Effect (1928), C.V. Raman
1 Å = 10⁻¹⁰ m (length); decibel = sound level; pascal = pressure
KE = p²/2m – doubling momentum quadruples KE (+300%)
Tungsten = filament (very high melting point); fuse wire = low melting point
Einstein's Nobel (1921) – photoelectric effect, not relativity
Atmakur (Anantapur) – first artificial-rain experiment keyed for AP (asked 2008 and 2010)
CTRI Rajahmundry; CCMB and ICRISAT Hyderabad; NIO Goa; CPCRI Kasaragod
LIGO-India lead institutes: IPR Gandhinagar, IUCAA Pune, RRCAT Indore (DAE + DST)
NATMO Kolkata – attached office of DST; digital embossing for braille maps
India: GII 2023 rank 40; NRI 2023 rank 60; IP Index 2024 rank 42/55
Rhodamine-B – the dye behind Tamil Nadu's 2024 cotton-candy ban
WIDUSHI – DST support for senior women scientists
checklist: Is it a unit/instrument? Fix the dimension first.
Is a formula hiding behind it (KE, magnification)? Compute, don't guess.
For institutes: match the institute to its crop/ecosystem and parent ministry.
Statement sets: mark each T/F, then re-read 'correct' vs 'incorrect'.
Recent devices: decode the name, then confirm the developer.
